Fill your graveyard with creatures, including Bringer of the Last Gift. Then cast Superior Spider-Man for 4 mana and have him enter as a copy of Bringer. Bringer's effect only works "if you cast it." You did cast Spider-Man, so the copy's effect should fire, though I'm reading the card text here and couldn't test it. Every other creature on the battlefield, yours and the opponent's, gets sacrificed. Then every creature card that was already in a graveyard comes back. Your milled Town Greeters, Overlords and Kioras return and trigger their "enters" effects again, and you keep a 4/4 flier.

**Key cards**
- **Town Greeter (4):** Mills four and puts a land into your hand. If that land is a Town, you also gain 2 life; Starting Town is the deck's Town. When Bringer brings it back, it mills four more.

- **Cache Grab (4) and Dredger's Insight (2):** Each mills four and gets a card back. Insight also gains you 1 life whenever creature cards leave your graveyard, which both Spider-Man and Bringer do.
- **Ways to get Bringer into the graveyard:**
  - Kiora (draw two, discard two)
  - Bitter Triumph (discard a card as its cost)
  - Molt Tender (mills one a turn, and also makes mana)
- **Glarb:** Lets you cast Spider-Man or Bringer straight off the top of your library, and surveils 2.
- **Spider-Man flexibility:** He can copy any creature card in a graveyard. A 4-mana Overlord is a good fallback when Bringer isn't there.
- **Removal (8):** 3 Bitter Triumph, 2 Assassin's Trophy, 2 Fell, 1 Shoot the Sheriff.

**Odds**
With no mulligans, you have a Spider-Man in hand by turn 4 on the play only 52.8% of the time, and 60.1% by turn 6. You're almost certain (99.4%) to have one of the 22 graveyard-filling cards by turn 4. Spider-Man is the bottleneck. Many of them can be cast more than once, through warp, Adventures (cards with a second spell half) or airbending, so each body gets you a card, a removal spell or a token. - 3 Appa, Steadfast Guardian, 2 Exalted Sunborn, 2 Aang, the Last Airbender
- 4 Airbender Ascension, 2 Virtue of Loyalty, 4 Get Lost
- 4 Temple Garden, 4 Overgrown Farmland, 2 Lush Portico, 6 Plains, 6 Forest

- **Airbender Ascension:** It gets a counter each time one of your creatures enters. At four or more counters, it exiles and returns a creature at your end step. The best targets:
  - All-Fates Stalker: the creature it had exiled comes back, then it exiles a new target, which is usually the better one.
  - Woodland Acolyte: draws a card every time.
  - Starfield Shepherd: searches out a Plains or a 1-mana creature (like Llanowar Elves) every time.
- **Warp creatures** (All-Fates Stalker, Starfield Shepherd, Haliya, Exalted Sunborn): Warp lets you cast them cheap from your hand, then they go to exile at end of turn and you can cast them again later. That second cast is a spell from exile, so it triggers Appa. They also enter twice for Ascension.
- **Appa, Steadfast Guardian:** It has flash. When it enters, it airbends any of your other nonland permanents. Airbended cards go to exile and you can recast them for {2}. Its Adventure half, Fetch Quest, costs 7 normally. It mills seven cards and puts a creature, enchantment or land from them onto the battlefield, so it can hit Appa, Sunborn or a land. **The plan**
You trade removal and flying creatures with the opponent early, then cast Doomsday Excruciator (6/6 flier, costs BBBBBB). When you cast it, each player exiles all but the bottom six cards of their library. From then on the game ends fast. Either the 6/6 flier kills them, or Insatiable Avarice finishes their library: its "target player draws three cards and loses 3 life" mode works on the opponent.

**Why the key cards**
- **Doomsday Excruciator (3 copies):** The finisher. It draws you an extra card every upkeep, and it's a Demon, which matters for the next two cards.
- **Insatiable Avarice (4):**
  - Before Excruciator, the tutor mode ({B}+{2}) puts Excruciator on top of your library.
  - After it, the {B}+{BB} mode makes the opponent draw 3 from their six-card library.
  - Cast during your turn with Bloodletter of Aclazotz out, the 3 life loss becomes 6. Bloodletter doubles any life an opponent loses during your turn.
  - With the 4 Avarice, you have about an 81% chance to have Excruciator or Avarice by turn 6 on the play.
- **Archenemy's Charm (3):** BBB instant with three modes:
  - Exile a creature or planeswalker.
  - Return Excruciator (or Bloodletter) from your graveyard to hand after removal. Casting Excruciator again cuts libraries back to six.
  - Give a creature two +1/+1 counters and lifelink to win a race.
- **Demon support:** Unholy Annex drains 2 at your end step if you control a Demon, and Bloodletter and Excruciator are both Demons. With Bloodletter out that drain becomes 4.
- **Feldon's Cane (1):** The catch is that Excruciator cuts your library to six too. You draw at least 2 a turn (upkeep plus draw step, more with Annex), while the opponent draws 1. So you only get a few turns to finish them. Cane shuffles your graveyard back into your library, which stretches your clock and theirs doesn't. Avarice can tutor for it.
- **The shell:** Deep-Cavern Bat, Preacher of the Schism, Qarsi Revenant, Bitter Triumph, Shoot the Sheriff and Stab are all heavily played in Mono-Black and Dimir right now.

**How to play Excruciator**
Cast it when the opponent can't race a 6/6 flier and can't counter it. Don't cast it when you're low on life or your graveyard is small, unless you have Avarice ready to point at them. Once it's down, don't make any draws you don't need.

**The mana**
25 lands: 21 Swamp, 3 Realm of Koh and 1 Soulstone Sanctuary, so 24 of them make black. Real Mono-Black lists average about 24 lands with 21 black sources. I went one land higher and cut colorless lands down to a single Sanctuary because of the six-drop that needs BBBBBB. With 24 black sources you're 99.9% likely to see at least one by turn 6. check_deck reported no issues.

**Sideboarding against the current field**
- **Simic Ouroboroid (18%) and Landfall (14%):** Bring in Day of Black Sun, Nowhere to Run and Long Goodbye. Take out Feldon's Cane and 1–2 Avarice.
- **Dimir Midrange and Jeskai Control:** Bring in Duress and Intimidation Tactics to clear the way for Excruciator. Take out Stab and Shoot the Sheriff.
- **Izzet and Boros Aggro:** Bring in Long Goodbye, Day of Black Sun and Nowhere to Run. Cut Feldon's Cane and an Excruciator, and keep Bat and Qarsi Revenant in for lifelink.
- **Reanimator and Lessons:** Bring in Soul-Guide Lantern and Strategic Betrayal (both exile the graveyard), plus Duress where it hits something.

**What I couldn't verify**
None of the three cards you asked for show up much in results. Each appears in only 2–7 lists in the last 90 days, so how this deck matches up is untested. I also didn't check exactly how many opposing decks can handle a 6/6 flier or come back from a six-card library.

I submitted **UR Welder-Cam Combo**, a Vintage **brew**. None of the three cards appears in any Vintage list from the last 90 days, so there was no proven version to copy.

## The plan
These three cards make an infinite-damage combo. Put Goblin Welder on the battlefield with one of the two artifacts in play and the other in your graveyard. Say Sewer-veillance Cam is in play and Legion Extruder is in the graveyard:
1. Tap Welder to swap them. Cam leaving the battlefield untaps Welder, and Extruder entering deals 2 damage.
2. Tap Welder to swap them back. Cam entering untaps Welder again.
3. Repeat. You deal 2 damage per loop for as long as you like.

Welder has to have been under your control since your turn started (no summoning sickness) for the first tap. After that, Cam handles every untap. If you're missing a piece, you can play fair: Extruder's 2 damage on entry kills small creatures, Cam can flash in to tap a blocker or attacker, and Cam can also sacrifice itself to draw two cards.

## Why the key cards
- **Goblin Welder ×4, Legion Extruder ×4, Sewer-veillance Cam ×4:** the combo itself.
- **Goblin Engineer ×3:** when it enters, it searches your library for any artifact and puts it straight into your graveyard. That covers both the missing piece and the graveyard setup in one card.
- **Ways to get the other artifact into the graveyard:**
  - Thirst for Knowledge ×3 lets you discard an artifact.
  - Cam's own sacrifice ability puts it there.
  - Extruder can sacrifice another artifact (including Cam) to make a 3/3 Golem.
  - Tinker sacrifices an artifact as part of its cost. Sacrificing Cam to Tinker for Extruder sets up the whole loop in one spell.
- **Tutors:**
  - Trinket Mage finds Cam (it searches for mana value 1 or less).
  - Tribute Mage finds Extruder (mana value 2).
  - Fabricate finds either one.
  - Mystical Tutor finds Tinker or Thirst.
  - Karn, the Great Creator can grab sideboard artifacts like Wurmcoil Engine, Tormod's Crypt, Pithing Needle or Grafdigger's Cage. Its passive ability also shuts off the opponent's artifact abilities, which hurts Shops.
- **Honest odds:** with no mulligans and no draw spells, you'll have Welder plus an Extruder source plus a Cam source by turn 4 on the play about **28%** of the time. Welder is the bottleneck: you see it only 53% of the time, and nothing else does exactly what it does. I checked Scrap Welder, and it can't loop because it only returns artifacts cheaper than the one it sacrifices. Ancestral Recall, Brainstorm, Ponder, Timetwister and the Thirsts are there to dig for it.
- I left out Vexing Bauble even though most of the field plays it. It counters any spell cast without spending mana, which includes your own Moxen, Black Lotus, Mana Crypt and Force of Will cast for free.

## The mana
- 14 lands:
  - 4 Volcanic Island and 3 Island
  - 6 fetch lands: 2 Scalding Tarn, plus 1 each of Flooded Strand, Polluted Delta, Misty Rainforest and Bloodstained Mire
  - Urza's Saga, which searches for Moxen, Sol Ring or Mana Crypt
- 9 pieces of fast mana: Black Lotus, all five Moxen, Sol Ring, Mana Crypt and Mana Vault. The off-color Moxen still count as artifacts for your artifact synergies.
- The land count is close to Lurrus PO (14.5 on average); I compared against it with the deck checker. The checker counted 14 blue and 10 red sources, which is low on blue compared with PO (16.6). I didn't change the fetch lands any further, and I didn't check whether the checker counts Bloodstained Mire as a blue source.

## Sideboarding
- **Lurrus Control / Lurrus PO / Paradoxical Outcome (about 45% of the field):** bring in 2 Pyroblast, Red Elemental Blast and Flusterstorm. Add Mindbreak Trap against PO. Take out Lightning Bolt and Tribute Mage.
- **Raker and Sphere Shops (21%):** bring in 2 Abrade, Fiery Confluence and Hurkyl's Recall. Hurkyl's can also return your own artifacts to your hand if you need to reuse them. Take out Pyroblast, Mental Misstep and Force of Negation.
- **Dredge (7%):** bring in Soul-Guide Lantern, Grafdigger's Cage and Tormod's Crypt. The Cage doesn't stop Welder, because it only stops creature cards entering from graveyards. Be careful with Crypt: it can only exile one player's graveyard, so aim it at theirs, never yours.
- **Mono-White Initiative:** bring in Lightning Bolt, Abrade and Fiery Confluence. Extruder's 2 damage on entry is already good here.
- **Oath:** bring in Pithing Needle (or get it with Karn) and Pyroblasts.

## What I couldn't verify
The combo's timing comes from how I read the card text: the Welder swap happens all at once, then Cam's enter and leave triggers go on the stack. I'm confident in that reading, but I didn't check it against official rulings. The deck has no tournament results behind it, so expect to adjust the counts after you play it.

I've submitted a Boros (red-white) brew called **"Boros Eidolon Recursion."**

**The plan**
Play cheap creatures and spells that are more than one color (called multicolored, or gold). Both Eidolons say: "Whenever you cast a multicolored spell, you may return this card from your graveyard to your hand." So you can sacrifice them for their abilities, then cast a gold spell to get them back. Every card that leaves your graveyard also puts a +1/+1 counter on Spirit Mascot. Each Eidolon comes back on its own trigger, so returning both should give Mascot two counters.

**Decklist (60)**
- **Creatures (27):** 4 Spirit Mascot, 4 Burning-Tree Emissary, 4 Wojek Halberdiers, 4 Kor Skyfisher, 3 Skyknight Legionnaire, 4 Aurora Eidolon, 4 Sandstorm Eidolon
- **Spells (15):** 4 Manamorphose, 4 Lightning Bolt, 2 Fire at Will, 3 Journey to Nowhere, 2 Prismatic Strands
- **Lands (18):** 4 Wind-Scarred Crag, 2 Boros Garrison, 7 Mountain, 5 Plains

**Key cards**
- **The Eidolons:** they're weak as 2/2s for 4 mana, but you get them back over and over.
  - Sandstorm Eidolon ({R}, sacrifice it: target creature can't block this turn) clears a blocker for a big attack.
  - Aurora Eidolon ({W}, sacrifice it: prevent the next 3 damage to any target) saves Mascot from a Lightning Bolt or wins a fight.
- **Spirit Mascot:** it's gold itself, so casting it brings back any Eidolons already in your graveyard. Prismatic Strands also grows it, because casting it again with flashback (by tapping a white creature) makes it leave the graveyard.
- **Ways to cast gold spells (21 in total):**
  - **Manamorphose:** pays for itself (it adds two mana), draws a card and still counts as multicolored, so it's basically a free Eidolon rebuy.
  - **Burning-Tree Emissary:** red-green hybrid, castable with red mana alone. It makes its {R}{G} back, which can pay for Manamorphose.
  - **Fire at Will:** a removal spell that also counts as gold.
  - **Wojek Halberdiers and Skyknight Legionnaire:** common red-white creatures.
- **Kor Skyfisher:** returns an Eidolon or Emissary to your hand so you can use it again, or picks up a Boros Garrison to replay it.
- **Odds:** you have about an 82% chance to see an Eidolon by turn 5 (on the play) and a 99.5% chance to see a gold spell.

**Mana**
- 18 lands: 13 red sources and 11 white. The red tilt helps cast Burning-Tree Emissary with {R}{R} and keeps Bolt online.
- The dual lands are borrowed from the Boros Synthesizer deck. The deck checker flagged that Synthesizer runs about 20.5 lands. I ignored that, because those lists run extra artifact lands for their artifact synergies. This deck's average mana value is 2.45, and the checker recommends 17.7 lands, so 18 is right.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Madness (16%) and Mono-Red Rally:** bring in Circle of Protection: Red (2) and Electrickery (2). Prismatic Strands naming red is already in the main deck.
- **Affinity and Synthesizer:** bring in Dust to Dust (3) and Cast into the Fire (2).
- **Faeries, UW Familiars, Jeskai Control and Spy Combo:** bring in Pyroblast (2) and Red Elemental Blast (2).
- **Elves:** bring in Electrickery and Cast into the Fire.
- **Terror, Golgari Gardens and other graveyard decks:** bring in Relic of Progenitus (2). Tapping it to exile a card from your own graveyard also grows Mascot.
- **What to take out:** usually Fire at Will (it only hits attacking or blocking creatures) and a Skyknight. Against fast decks, cut a Sandstorm Eidolon.

**Label and caveats**
- This is a brew. None of the three named cards showed up in any recent Pauper results.
- Lightning Helix, Boros Charm and Boros Swiftblade would fit perfectly, but the card tool shows they aren't legal in Pauper.
- Lobber Crew (untaps whenever you cast a multicolored spell) is another option if you want a slower version.
- I haven't play-tested whether a 4-mana 2/2 plan holds up against Madness's speed.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
This is a brew: **BG Living Death**, built on the mana and interaction of the BG Survival deck.

**The plan**
Spend turns 1–3 stripping the opponent's hand with Duress and Cabal Therapy while you fill your own graveyard with fatties. Then cast Living Death (5 mana: {3}{B}{B}). It sacrifices every creature on the battlefield, theirs and yours, and returns every creature card from both graveyards. That's a one-sided board wipe that also hands you a team of 6/6s. Living Death shows up in only 7 lists in the last 90 days (0.3% of results), mostly as a one-of in BG Survival, so this deck is the untested version that runs four copies.

**Key cards**
- **Ways to fill your graveyard:**
  - Buried Alive puts three creatures in at once.
  - Survival of the Fittest discards a creature to find another, so every activation feeds the graveyard.
  - Wild Mongrel can discard for free, which also lets you get rid of fatties you draw.
  - Krosan Tusker and Twisted Abomination cycle themselves into the yard and fetch you a land.
- **Off-color fatties: Akroma, Angel of Wrath and Phantom Nishoba.** Living Death doesn't care what color a creature is, so these are pure graveyard targets. You never cast them. Akroma comes back as a 6/6 flier with haste and protection from black and red. Nishoba gains you life from every hit, which is huge against Sligh and Goblins.
- **Creatures that do something when they come back:**
  - Deranged Hermit returns with four Squirrels.
  - Bone Shredder returns and kills one of their creatures that came back too.
  - Verdant Force makes a token every upkeep.
  - Squee is fodder you can discard to Survival every turn, and he returns to your hand each upkeep.
- **Finding Living Death and casting it early:** Diabolic Intent (sacrifice a Birds of Paradise you're done with) is the only legal tutor that can find it. Demonic Tutor isn't legal in Premodern and Vampiric Tutor is banned. You see Living Death or Intent by turn 4 about 68% of the time, and Living Death plus a graveyard filler about 66% of the time. Dark Ritual can get Living Death out on turn 3.

**Mana**
20 lands (4 Llanowar Wastes, 8 Swamp, 8 Forest), plus 4 Birds of Paradise, 3 Dark Ritual and 4 creatures that cycle for a land. The deck check passed. It warned about white and red sources for Akroma and Squee, but you never intend to cast either. Real BG Survival lists average 21.25 lands. If you keep getting stuck on four mana, swap a Duress for a 21st land.

**Sideboard, by the decks the meta shows most**
- **Stiflenought (14.9%):** bring in Smother and Diabolic Edict. Smother kills Phyrexian Dreadnought because its mana value is 1. Living Death also deals with a Dreadnought on the battlefield. Be careful if one is in their graveyard: it comes back and they can Stifle its trigger again.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** bring in Engineered Plague (name Goblin) and Pernicious Deed. Count both graveyards before you cast Living Death against Goblins, because their dead creatures come back too.
- **Enchantress and Replenish:** bring in Naturalize, Pernicious Deed and the 4th Duress.
- **Hermit Druid, Reanimator and Oath:** bring in Tormod's Crypt. It works well with this deck: exile their graveyard right before you cast Living Death. Uktabi Orangutan is an artifact answer you can fetch with Survival.
- **Cuts when siding in:** usually the 2nd Cabal Therapy, Squee and a Twisted Abomination.

**Weak points and what I couldn't check**
- Graveyard hate (Tormod's Crypt is in about 43% of recent lists) is your worst enemy. Against it, use Survival to find Mongrel, Hermit and Shredder and win with hard-cast creatures.
- I haven't playtested this list. The sideboard plans and the 20-land count are my judgment, not results from real lists.
